memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Cain said to the Lord, "My punishment is more than I can bear. Today you are driving me from the land, and I will be hidden from your presence; I will be a restless wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me." - Gen 4:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Cain finally speaks of his pain - "My punishment is more than I can bear." But listen closely to what grieves him. He mourns the consequences, not the sin. He is sorry he was caught, sorry he must wander, sorry he is afraid - but there is no word of sorrow for the brother he killed. His deepest dread is being "hidden from your presence."

There is a kind of regret that is really just self-pity. It cries about the results of sin without ever repenting of the sin itself. Scripture calls this "worldly sorrow," and it leads nowhere good, while "godly sorrow brings repentance" that leads to life (2 Cor 7:10).

Yet even here, something aches in Cain's words - to be hidden from God's presence is a heavy loss. Deep down, the human heart knows it was made for God and cannot thrive apart from Him.

The wonderful truth of the gospel is that in Christ, no repentant sinner is ever driven from God's presence. Jesus was forsaken on the cross so that we might never be cast out (John 6:37). The wanderer can come home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you sorry for your sin, or only for its consequences?
- Does being far from God's presence grieve your heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me godly sorrow that leads to true repentance, not mere regret. Thank You that in Christ I am never cast out of Your presence.
